correctness.rationale: For posterior Beta(A,B) and k future observations, Qk=(B)_k/(A+B)_k. For each deterministic adapted rule pi, the ratio Hpi/Qk is a finite nonnegative sum over successful future words of (A)_r/(B+k-r)_r; hence the optimal ratio is continuous strictly increasing A, strictly decreasing B, with endpoint range 0 to infinity, giving unique A_c(B,k) increasing B. First-future-success policy has ratio kA/(B+k-1) so A_c lies below this line. An induction on k proves optimality of first-future-success when B>=k(k-1)+1 and kA<=B+k-1; below that shape boundary, a legal one-step adaptation after an immediate success strictly improves on nominal line, establishing sharp necessity. At k=2, comparing two distinct legal policies gives the exact square-root-versus-linear minimum.
residual_risks: One right, deterministic finite horizon k>=1, Beta(A,B)>0 posterior at currently observed success, Bernoulli exchangeability conditional on fixed p. No universal fixed calendar cutoff or general non-Beta posterior result.
